reading.body:
The DāStor facility at 3400 Horizon Drive in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania is a 22,000 square foot data center rated for 4 MW of power delivery. This places it at rank 4 among the four Pennsylvania facilities with published capacity figures, accounting for 18 percent of the state's total published data center capacity of 22.2 MW. Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data center facilities overall, suggesting most operators in the state do not publish power specifications.

At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, the 4 MW IT load would support roughly 100 racks, though the actual mix depends on whether the facility hosts training clusters, inference, or other workloads not specified in the published data. The campus's power-to-footprint ratio of 182 watts per square foot is moderate for data center colocation, leaving uncertain how much of the 4 MW serves customer compute versus facility systems. No certifications, tenant roster, or grid interconnection details are published.

The facility matters to AI scaling only if Pennsylvania's thin 22.2 MW of published capacity masks substantial unpublished capacity, or if this site's customer mix includes large model training. The state currently ranks far below major AI data center hubs and no operator in Pennsylvania has published figures approaching the 100+ MW campuses now standard for frontier compute. This facility is a marginal contributor to national AI infrastructure based on the facts available.
